analysis: The only changed file is docs/developer/test.md, a documentation-only edit. The supplied changes are a date bump (line 3), a new test command `python3 scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py` in the tooling checks list (head ~1289), and an expanded description (head ~1325-1340, truncated in the excerpt) of the release publication and cluster runtime model-metadata tests. The base units reviewed are the surrounding unchanged text, with no executable code, configuration, workflow or key-handling changes. The new description says the tests run against a local HTTP registry, read no weights and use no network, and that registration sends the cluster_runtime block in canonical form and rejects oversized or malformed blocks, including a 64 KiB registration body limit. These are consistent with the existing threat model (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011, A-011, A-017) and add no new attack surface. Neither the changed block's implementing scripts (scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh) nor the provider registration code were supplied, so I could not verify those claims. The patch excerpt is truncated at the end of the new paragraph, so the rest of the new doc text is unseen. This is a documentation claim, not a security regression. Integration should check that the new cluster_runtime registration block (grants, parity qualifications) is validated server-side and covered by the threat model, since this PR's doc references it but the implementing code was not in this batch.
